headline: Homelessness pilot program and airport hangar lease approved; 17 Green Street added to park list.
summary: Lori Smith was confirmed as city manager and starts December 29. Staff presented a $954,211 Community Development Block Grant plan and a proposed change to the Adam's Point tax increment financing deal. A public hearing on the Adam's Point change is set for November 17, and one on the block grant plan for December 15.
decisions: Approved appointment of Lori Smith as city manager, starting December 29, unanimously.
Approved appointments of Paul Matthews (Ward 4) and Kate Snow (Ward 2) to the Public Art Commission, unanimously.
Approved first reading of an ordinance to fold the Project Canopy Committee into the Sustainability Commission, unanimously.
Approved airport leases, including a three-year hangar lease for Rampside Aviation, unanimously.
Approved homelessness pilot program, using a $25,000 set-aside and opioid settlement funds, unanimously.
Passed as an emergency ordinance adding 59 South Street and 17 Green Street to the Cannon Plaza park listing, unanimously.
Approved amendment separating the council rules from Appendix A, unanimously.
Approved moving City Council standing committees into the Code of Ordinances under Division 19, unanimously.
discussion: Adam's Point tax increment deal: Members asked how the proposed $68,791 annual cap would work and how inflation affects long-term projections, which staff called estimates.
Homelessness pilot program: Members asked how often staff would report back and whether staff recommend the program. A resident urged leaders to walk downtown and see conditions for themselves.
Cannon Plaza listing: Discussion focused on enforcement at the Green Street lot, where encampments and dumping have occurred, and on whether the change should take effect right away.
Waterfront pier comments: A resident told the council that the harbor masters' recommended site was better and questioned the state's review of alternatives.
